waivers.text:
SLEEPER — FAAB: $87 of $100 remaining (waiver_budget_used ticked up to $13, so a $1 minimum claim went through since last check). This is a Wednesday processing day, and the board looks different than it did Tuesday — Ollie Gordon, Kenyon Sadiq, and Keaton Mitchell (all recommended last run) are now ROSTERED by other teams in this league; they cleared waivers before you got to them. Fresh top targets, cross-checked against every roster in Gangstas Paradise so these are confirmed actually available:
1. Tyler Higbee (TE, LAR) — the best fix for your real TE hole. Strange is fine as a starter but Darnell Washington (your only backup) is buried on Pittsburgh's depth chart behind Freiermuth and has zero standalone value. Higbee gives you an actual streamable body. Drop Darnell Washington. FAAB $10.
2. Keenan Allen (WR, IND) — Josh Downs' running mate at WR2 for the Colts, a real target earner if Downs ever misses time and cheap insurance for a deep WR room. Drop Woody Marks (buried third string in Houston's backfield, no standalone path). FAAB $5.
3. Jaylen Wright (RB, MIA, Questionable) — speculative but live: Miami's backfield behind Achane has real weekly upside if Wright is ever the lead. Drop Devaughn Vele (healthy but a buried WR4 in New Orleans). FAAB $4.
4. Isaiah Davis (RB, NYJ) — dart throw for RB depth if the Jets' timeshare ever tilts his way. Only if you want a 6th bench RB — skip if you'd rather stand pat. FAAB $2.
5. Browns DEF (CLE) — forward-looking stream, not for this week. Flagging it now because your Week 7 problem (JAX + LAC both on bye that week, wiping out your DEF AND your Herbert/Hampton) needs a plan; worth a speculative low bid to have in your pocket. FAAB $3.
Total if you take all five: $24, leaving ~$63 banked for the actual Week 7 bye scramble and any Week 12 trade-deadline pushes.
Hold, don't drop: Stefon Diggs and Tyler Shough — same read as always, Diggs is still WAS's real WR2 by depth chart and Shough is your Week 7 QB streamer once Herbert's Week 7 bye hits (separately from the LAC bye — don't confuse the two).

YAHOO — still no access to your free-agent pool (private league, no login), and the newest screenshot in your Drive folder is now 17 days old (Sept 13). Same two names worth checking availability on yourself: a TE stream to pair with Isaiah Likely, and a depth RB behind Corum now that Etienne's hamstring has dragged into a second-plus week. Drop a fresh free-agent screenshot (Players > Available) plus your Week 1-3 final scores into the War room folder and next run can give you real bid guidance and finally backfill your season tracker.

season.lesson: Started Josh Downs (5.7) over Stefon Diggs sitting on the bench (15.5) in the flex — 9.8 points left on the table. Separately, Zay Flowers' 26-point day ended in a hamstring re-injury that's now clouding Week 2; watch practice reports closely on players who leave games early even when the box score looks great.

Tyler Shough (22.38, waiver QB stash) outscored started QB Justin Herbert (9.88) by 12.5 — not a real swap given Shough's a Saints starter you don't play, but the bigger miss was starting Michael Wilson (3.8) over bench WR Josh Downs (14.2), a 10.4-point gap; the Week 3 lineup already has that fixed. Also: Zay Flowers stayed rostered through a scoreless Week 2 (ruled Out, no IR move) — a wasted bench spot two weeks running.

Michael Wilson (25.9) outscored started Josh Downs (12.7) by 13.2 on the bench — the second straight week a bench WR beat a starter by double digits. Backup QB Tyler Shough (24.8) also beat Herbert (13.74) again. Tempting as that pattern looks, don't chase last week's points by benching your clearly better asset — see this week's Do Now, where that exact overcorrection is sitting live in your Week 4 lineup.
